questions.q: Can a single node run more than one Executor?
options: Yes — a node with enough CPU cores and memory can run several independent Executor processes at once
No, exactly one Executor per node, always

questions.q: What is the difference between scaling up and scaling out?
options: Scaling up means fewer, bigger nodes; scaling out means more, smaller nodes
They are exactly the same thing with different names
Scaling up only applies to storage, never compute
Scaling out means removing nodes from the cluster
questions.explain: Both increase total capacity, but they trade off differently in terms of fault tolerance and network overhead.

questions.q: Why might more, smaller nodes (scaling out) be more fault-tolerant than fewer, bigger nodes?
options: Losing one node loses a smaller fraction of total capacity, compared to losing one of only a few large nodes
Smaller nodes never fail, unlike larger ones
There is no real fault-tolerance difference between the two approaches
Fewer, bigger nodes are always more fault-tolerant instead
questions.explain: This ties directly back to Lesson 29's discussion of fault tolerance in distributed systems.
